items.quote: And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together
items.claim: On the second day after he went out, Moses saw two Hebrew men fighting each other.

items.quote: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
items.claim: Moses stepped in and asked the man in the wrong why he was hitting his fellow Hebrew.

items.quote: Who made thee a prince and a judge over us?
items.claim: The Hebrew in the wrong rejected Moses' right to act as a ruler or judge over them.

items.quote: intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian?
items.claim: The Hebrew man showed he knew Moses had killed an Egyptian. He asked whether Moses meant to kill him the same way.
items.mechanism: reference to Moses' earlier killing of an Egyptian

items.quote: And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.
items.claim: Moses became afraid once he realized his killing of the Egyptian had become known.
items.object: exposure of the killing of the Egyptian
items.mechanism: realization that the deed was publicly known
